newsitem.title: INDIA: PROFIT-TAKING, POLITICAL JITTERS HIT DELHI SHARES.
newsitem.headline: PROFIT-TAKING, POLITICAL JITTERS HIT DELHI SHARES.

text.p: Delhi shares extended losses to close lower on Friday as firms pocketed profits amid political worries, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index, which had opened with modest gains, closed down 7.93 points at 935.37.
Traders said settlement on the Bombay bourse and hectic selling of index-weighted stocks wiped out the early gains.
"Foreign players with huge positions in key stocks preferred to offload shares at higher levels," Ashok Kaul of stock brokers Rajpaul Chadha said.

Also weighing on values were concerns over the government's stability after it suffered two humiliating setbacks in parliament, including being forced to withdraw an insurance bill in the face of opposition from parties on the Right and Left.
"The prevailing adverse political situation also had an impact on market sentiment," a stock broker said.
Reliance Industries surged to 374.20 rupees on early speculative buying but ended the day at 372.35 due to selling by profit-takers.
Ranbaxy Laboratories shot up 25 rupees to 775 on rumours of a bonus issue.
Hindustan Lever dropped 17 rupees to to 1,526.
